verses.zh: 这麦基洗德就是撒冷王，又是至高　神的祭司，本是长远为祭司的。他当亚伯拉罕杀败诸王回来的时候，就迎接他，给他祝福。
verses.en: Now this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, met Abraham as he was returning from defeating the kings and blessed him.[NOTE:1]
notes: A series of quotations from Gen 14:17-19.
verses.commentary:
7:1 "Melchizedek" He was a Gentile king/priest of the old Canaanite city then called Salem, which later
became Jebus and then later Jerusalem (cf. Heb. 5:6,10; 6:20; 7:1,11,17). His name means "king of righteousness." His lineage is
never mentioned, but Abraham pays homage to him. This is why he is such an appropriate OT type for Jesus Christ. He is only mentioned
in Gen. 14:18-20 and Ps. 110:4. There has been much discussion about his identity.

- for Philo, he is a figure of the human soul

- for Origen, he is an angel

- for Ambrose, he is the angel of the Lord

- for others, he is the national angel of Israel, Michael

- for Epiphanius, he is the incarnation of Holy Spirit

- for the Melchizedekites, he is greater than the Messiah and all prayer goes through him

- for some Jews, Jerome and Luther, he is Shem, Noah's son

Melchizedek is used as a type of Jesus' priesthood for several reasons:

- his name ‒ King of Righteousnes

- he blessed Abraham (i.e., a greater blesses a lesser)

- Abraham offered a tithe to him (inferiors always tithe to superiors) and by rabbinical hermeneutics
thereby Levi also offered a tithe (cf. Heb. 7:4-9)

- his parents are not listed, so rabbinical theology said he was without parents and thereby eternal
(cf. Heb. 7:3; Ps. 110:4b)

- he was king in the later holy city, Jerusalem (Salem, cf. Gen. 14:18)

- he was a priest of God Most High (i.e., El Elyon, cf. Gen. 14:18)

- he allows the author to establish a legitimate priesthood apart from the Levitical Priesthood

SPECIAL TOPIC: MELCHIZEDEK

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALEM

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, B.

▣ "king. . .priest" He is the only person in the OT who combines royalty and priesthood (i.e.,
Psalm 110). In Zechariah 3 and 4 two leaders, Zerubbabel and Joshua, are united as both royal (line of David)
and priest (line of Aaron) post exilic leaders in the restored Jerusalem.

▣ "of the Most High God" This title is often used by non-Israelites. Israelites were not the only ones
who YHWH had revealed Himself to. There were several outside the family of Abraham who knew, worshiped, and
followed YHWH (here Elyon, BDB 751, KB 832).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, B.

▣ "and blessed him" The greater blesses the lesser; therefore, Abraham (and by rabbinical
implications his descendant, Levi), was blessed by Melchizedek (cf. Gen. 14:19), which shows his superiority
over the Aaronic priesthood. It also shows that Jesus, who was from the line of Judah, could be a priest
of a different order.

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕也将自己所得来的，取十分之一给他。他头一个名翻出来就是仁义王，他又名撒冷王，就是平安王的意思。
verses.en: To him[NOTE:1] also Abraham apportioned a tithe[NOTE:2] of everything.[NOTE:3] His name first means[NOTE:4] king of righteousness, then king of Salem,[NOTE:5] that is, king of peace.
notes: Grk “to whom,” continuing the description of Melchizedek. Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Or “a tenth part.”
A quotation from Gen 14:20.
Grk “first being interpreted,” describing Melchizedek.
These words are repeated from the quotation of Gen 14:18 in the previous verse.
verses.commentary:
7:2 "a tenth" Notice that the tithe (cf. Gen. 14:20) is older than the Mosaic law. It was a way like
the Sabbath and first fruits of showing God's ownership of all (cf. Gen. 14:19c).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TITHING IN THE MOSAIC LEGISLATION

▣ "by the translation of his name" The specific etymology of the phrase "king of
righteousness" is uncertain but a similar title is used for the Messiah in Jer. 23:6 ("the Lord our
righteousness") and 33:16 ("the Lord is our righteousness"). Also, the Messiah will be righteous and bring
peace (cf. Isa. 9:6; 26:3,12; 32:17; and 54:10).

Notice Melchizedek goes by two titles.

- King of Righteousness

- King of Salem, which means "King of Peace"

▣ "King of righteousness" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "Salem" The city may have gotten its name from the Hebrew term shalom which means
"peace." Some scholars think it refers to a Jebusite deity. The city is called Salem in Genesis 14, but
Ps. 76:2 relates it to Jerusalem (i.e., Zion), which was called Jebus during the Canaanite period. It was captured by
King David amd made his capital.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALEM

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT)

verses.zh: 他无父，无母，无族谱，无生之始，无命之终，乃是与　神的儿子相似。
verses.en: Without father, without mother, without genealogy, he has neither beginning of days nor end of life but is like the son of God, and he remains a priest for all time.
verses.commentary:
7:3 This is rabbinical hermeneutics (midrash) based on the fact that Melchizedek's lineage is not given
in Gen. 14:18-20. Like all human beings Melchizedek had parents, but he serves as a type of the eternal Messiah
(cf. Heb. 7:8). This is developed in Heb. 7:8,12,16,17,21,24,25,28.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TYPOLOGY

SPECIAL TOPIC: RABBINICAL HERMENEUTICS

▣ "the Son of God"
SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF GOD

verses.zh: 你们想一想，先祖亚伯拉罕将自己所掳来上等之物取十分之一给他，这人是何等尊贵呢！
verses.en: But see how great he must be, if[NOTE:1] Abraham the patriarch gave him a tithe[NOTE:2] of his plunder.
notes: Grk “to whom.”
Or “a tenth part.”

verses.zh: 那得祭司职任的利未子孙，领命照例向百姓取十分之一，这百姓是自己的弟兄，虽是从亚伯拉罕身（原文是腰）中生的，还是照例取十分之一。
verses.en: And those of the sons of Levi who receive the priestly office[NOTE:1] have authorization according to the law to collect a tithe from the people, that is, from their fellow countrymen,[NOTE:2] although they, too, are descendants of Abraham.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “the priesthood.”
Grk “from their brothers.” See BDAG 18-19 s.v. ἀδελφός 2.b.
Grk “have come from the loins of Abraham.”
verses.commentary:
7:5 "although these are descended from Abraham" This is rabbinic logic based on Levi being present in
the loins of Abraham (cf. Heb. 7:10). This is Jewish exegesis, not scientific fact.

verses.zh: 独有麦基洗德，不与他们同谱，倒收纳亚伯拉罕的十分之一，为那蒙应许的亚伯拉罕祝福。
verses.en: But Melchizedek[NOTE:1] who does not share their ancestry[NOTE:2] collected a tithe[NOTE:3] from Abraham and blessed[NOTE:4] the one who possessed the promise.
notes: Grk “the one”; in the translation the referent (Melchizedek) has been specified for clarity.
Grk “is not descended from them.”
Or “a tenth part.”
The verbs “collected…and blessed” emphasize the continuing effect of the past actions, i.e., Melchizedek’s importance.

verses.zh: 从来位分大的给位分小的祝福，这是驳不倒的理。
verses.en: Now without dispute the inferior is blessed by the superior,
verses.commentary:
7:7 "the greater" The heart of the book of Hebrews is the comparison between the Mosaic covenant
and the new covenant in Christ.

This contrast is often expressed by the term "greater" (kreittōu/kreissōu),
which means "better," "superior," "more excellent," "more valuable," "higher rank." This is a recurrent key
theme in Hebrews.

- much better than the angels (cf. Heb. 1:4)

- better things concerning you (cf. Heb. 6:9)

- lesser is blessed by the greater (cf. Heb. 7:7)

- a better hope (cf. Heb. 7:19)

- a better covenant (cf. Heb. 7:22)

- a better covenant based on better promises (cf. Heb. 8:6)

- with better sacrifice (cf. Heb. 9:23)

- a better possession which abides (cf. Heb. 10:34)

- a better resurrection (cf. Heb. 11:35)

- a better country (cf. Heb. 11:16)

- God has provided something better (cf. Heb. 11:40)

- His sprinkled blood speaks better than Abel's (cf. Heb. 12:24)

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS IS GREATER THAN

verses.zh: 在这里收十分之一的都是必死的人；但在那里收十分之一的，有为他作见证的说，他是活的；
verses.en: and in one case tithes are received by mortal men, while in the other by him who is affirmed to be alive.
verses.commentary:
7:8 "lives on" This refers to the symbolic eternality of Melchizedek because

- his parents (genealogy) are not mentioned in Genesis 14 nor is his death recorded

- Ps. 110:4b's specific comment ("forever")

verses.zh: 并且可说那受十分之一的利未，也是藉着亚伯拉罕纳了十分之一。
verses.en: And it could be said that Levi himself, who receives tithes, paid a tithe through Abraham.
verses.commentary:
7:9-10 This is rabbinical exegesis. Since Levi the tribe of Aaron is descendant from Abraham, then
by analogy, the Jewish priesthood (i.e., even the High Priest) paid tithes to Melchizedek. Therefore,
Melchizedek is superior and Jesus is superior to Jewish priests.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS

verses.zh: 因为麦基洗德迎接亚伯拉罕的时候，利未已经在他先祖的身（原文是腰）中。
verses.en: For he was still in his ancestor Abraham’s loins[NOTE:1] when Melchizedek met him.
notes: Grk “in the loins of his father” (a reference to Abraham). The name “Abraham” has been repeated in the translation at this point (cf. v. 9) in order to clarify the referent (i.e., what ancestor was in view).sn The point of the phrase still in his ancestor’s loins is that Levi was as yet unborn, still in his ancestor Abraham’s body. Thus Levi participated in Abraham’s action when Abraham paid tithes to Melchizedek.

verses.zh: 从前百姓在利未人祭司职任以下受律法，倘若藉这职任能得完全，又何用另外兴起一位祭司，照麦基洗德的等次，不照亚伦的等次呢？
verses.en: So if perfection had in fact been possible through the Levitical priesthood—for on that basis[NOTE:1] the people received the law—what further need would there have been for another priest to arise, said to be in the order of Melchizedek and not in Aaron’s order?
notes: Grk “based on it.”
verses.commentary:
7:11 "if" This is a SECOND CLASS CONDITIONAL which is called contrary to fact. A false
statement is made to accentuate a false conclusion. The Levitical priesthood did not bring spiritual perfection or maturity.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS, VII

▣ "perfection" The Greek family of terms based on telos basically means "to bring to the
end," "to bring to completion," or "to bring to maturity" (cf. Heb. 5:11; 6:1; 7:19). This is a recurrent term. Here it refers to an adequate
and effective representative or intercessor.

SPECIAL TOPIC: END OR FULL (telos)

▣ "through the Levitical priesthood (for on the basis of it the people received the Law)" This
apparently refers to

- Moses being from the tribe of Levi and being God's messenger in giving the sacrificial system
of Israel

- the Levites and priests teaching the law to the people

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS

verses.zh: 祭司的职任既已更改，律法也必须更改。
verses.en: For when the priesthood changes, a change in the law must come[NOTE:1] as well.
notes: Grk “of necessity a change in the law comes to pass.”
verses.commentary:
7:12 "a change of law also" The purpose of the Mosaic law was never to produce righteousness, but to
show the continuing results of the fall and mankind's inability to please God (cf. Romans 7; Gal. 3:23-25). This is
a major truth in trying to figure out God's purpose for the Mosaic Law.

This phrase in context must refer to the "new covenant" (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEWS OF THE MOSAIC LAW

verses.zh: 因为这话所指的人本属别的支派，那支派里从来没有一人伺候祭坛。
verses.en: Yet the one these things are spoken about belongs to[NOTE:1] a different tribe, and no one from that tribe[NOTE:2] has ever officiated at the altar.
notes: Grk “shares in.”
Grk “from which no one.”
verses.commentary:
7:13 "from which no one has officiated at the altar" This is a PERFECT ACTIVE INDICATIVE,
which may imply that the sacrificial system was continuing. If so, Hebrews was written before Titus'
destruction of Jerusalem in A.D. 70. This seems logical because its destruction would be powerful
evidence of its inferiority to the New Covenant in Jesus.

No one outside the tribe of Levi and family of Aaron served as a priest in Jerusalem. This was
not the case in the Roman period of the occupation of Palestine (i.e., Annas, Caiaphas).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALTAR OF SACRIFICE

verses.zh: 我们的主分明是从犹大出来的；但这支派，摩西并没有提到祭司。
verses.en: For it is clear that our Lord is descended from Judah, yet Moses said nothing about priests in connection with that tribe.
verses.commentary:
7:14 "our Lord was descended from Judah" This is another PERFECT ACTIVE INDICATIVE. The
VERB "descend" means "sprang from" and is used for

- the rising of the sun (cf. Matt. 5:45)

- the movement of the planets (i.e., Rom. 8:39)

- plant shoots (i.e., imagery for Messiah, "Branch")

- as imagery for human descent (cf. Zech. 6:12; Isa. 11:1; Jer. 23:5-6)

Here it refers to Jacob's prophecies about his sons in Genesis 49 (esp. 49:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: The Branch of the Lord

▣ "Judah" Jesus was from the Davidic royal line of Judah (cf. Gen. 49:8-12; 2 Sam. 7:12-16;
Isa. 9:6,7; Matthew 1; Luke 3). Convincing Jews that Jesus was High Priest was so difficult because He was not of the priestly
tribe of Levi like Moses and Aaron.

verses.zh: 倘若照麦基洗德的样式，另外兴起一位祭司来，我的话更是显而易见的了。
verses.en: And this is even clearer if another priest arises in the likeness of Melchizedek,
verses.commentary:
7:15 "if" This is a FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE which is assumed to be true from
the author's perspective or for his literary purposes. Another priest has come and is from the line of
Melchizedek.

verses.zh: 他成为祭司，并不是照属肉体的条例，乃是照无穷（原文是不能毁坏）之生命的大能。
verses.en: who has become a priest not by a legal regulation about physical descent[NOTE:1] but by the power of an indestructible life.
notes: Grk “a law of a fleshly command.”
verses.commentary:
7:16

NASB
"not on the basis of a law of physical requirement"

NKJV, Peshitta
"not according to the laws of a fleshly commandment"

NRSV
"not through a legal requirement concerning physical descent"

TEV
"not by human rules and regulations"

NJB
"not in virtue of a law of physical descent"

Jesus' priestly authority does not rest in what tribe/family He descended from, but from
His possession of eternal, indestructible life (i.e., Melchizedek's parents are not named in Genesis 14
and the word "forever" is used in Ps. 110:4). Jesus has the endless life of God (as well as the oath and
promise of God).

▣

NASB, NRSV, NJB
"an indestructible life"

NKJV
"an endless life"

TEV
"a life that has no end"

Peshitta
"life which abides for ever"

This seems to be related to the rabbinical exegetical (Midrash) implication from
Ps. 110:4b that Melchizedek had no parents and, therefore, was eternal (cf. Heb. 7:6,8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RABBINICAL HERMENEUTICAL TECHNIQUES

verses.zh: 因为有给他作见证的说：「你是照着麦基洗德的等次永远为祭司。」
verses.en: For here is the testimony about him:[NOTE:1] “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “for he/it is witnessed that.”
A quotation from Ps 110:4 (see Heb 5:6 and 6:20).
verses.commentary:
7:17 "For it is attested of Him" This is a quote from the Septuagint of Ps. 110:4 (as is
Heb. 7:21).

▣ "Melchizedek" see

SPECIAL TOPIC: MELCHIZEDEK

verses.zh: 先前的条例，因软弱无益，所以废掉了，
verses.en: On the one hand a former command is set aside[NOTE:1] because it is weak and useless,[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “the setting aside of a former command comes to pass.”
Grk “because of its weakness and uselessness.”
verses.commentary:
7:18

NASB
"there is a setting aside"

NKJV
"there is an annulling"

NRSV
"the abrogation"

TEV
"is set aside"

NJB
"is thus abolished"

Peshitta
"the change that took place"

This term has been found in the Egyptian papyri (see J. H. Moulton and G. Milligan, Vocabulary
of the Greek Testament) in the sense of

- "to set aside"

- "to make null and void"

- "to be paid in full"

This verse speaks of the setting aside of a commandment (probably the physical lineage of
the high priest). It is rather shocking that an inspired OT passage (cf. Matt. 5:17-19) can be "set aside,"
yet this is exactly Paul's point in Galatians 3, in respect to the redemptive purpose of the law being set
aside. Paul, however, asserts that it was the weakness of fallen man (cf. Romans 1-3; 7), not the OT. The
author of Hebrews is showing the superiority of Jesus over Moses and calls the "Law" weak and useless
(cf. Heb. 8:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEW OF THE MOSAIC LAW

▣ "of a former commandment" This refers to the Levitical system or the Old Covenant characterized
by the Mosaic legislation and Aaron's priesthood.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SACRIFICIAL SYSTEM OF THE ANE

▣ "because of its weakness and uselessness" Hebrews 7:11; 8:13; Romans 1-3; 7; and Galatians 3 are
helpful in interpreting this phrase. It was not the Law of God, but human fallen nature that was weak and the Law was
unable to perform its restorative task!

verses.zh: （律法原来一无所成）就引进了更美的指望；靠这指望，我们便可以进到　神面前。
verses.en: for the law made nothing perfect. On the other hand a better hope is introduced, through which we draw near to God.
verses.commentary:
7:19 "(for the Law made nothing perfect)" Read Galatians 3. Here again is a word play on telos from Heb. 5:11;
6:1; 7:11,19,28), see full list in Contextual Insights, C. in chapter 10.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEW OF THE MOSAIC LAW

SPECIAL TOPIC: END OR FULL (telos)

▣ "better" See full note at Heb. 7:7.

▣ "through which we draw near to God" This is a key concept (cf. Heb. 7:25; 4:16; 10:1). The
author asserts that the Mosaic Law, with its Levitical priesthood and sacrifices, failed to bring humanity
to God, but Jesus, our High Priest, did not fail and will not fail (cf. Heb. 10:22; James 4:7).

Notice that Jesus brings a better covenant, but it is still a conditional covenant to which
humans must respond as the priests did (believers are now new covenant priests in a corporate sense (cf.
2 Pet. 2:5,9; Rev. 1:6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 再者，耶稣为祭司，并不是不起誓立的。
verses.en: And since[NOTE:1] this was not done without a sworn affirmation—for the others have become priests without a sworn affirmation,
notes: The Greek text contains an elaborate comparison between v. 20a and v. 22, with a parenthesis (vv. 20b-21) in between; the comparison is literally, “by as much as…by so much” or “to the degree that…to that same degree.”
verses.commentary:
7:20 "it was not without an oath" God's promises can be trusted because His character and
power stand behind them (cf. Isa. 46:10). This oath is a reference to Ps. 110:4, which is discussed in
Heb. 6:13-17.

verses.zh: 至于那些祭司，原不是起誓立的，只有耶稣是起誓立的；因为那立他的对他说：「主起了誓，决不后悔，你是永远为祭司。」
verses.en: but Jesus[NOTE:1] did so[NOTE:2] with a sworn affirmation by the one who said to him, “The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind, ‘You are a priest forever’”[NOTE:3]—
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The words “did so” are not in the Greek text, but are implied.
A quotation from Ps 110:4 (see Heb 5:6; 6:20, and 7:17).
verses.commentary:
7:21 This is another quote from the Septuagint of Ps. 110:4 (as is Heb. 7:17), which mentions an
"oath" by YHWH..

verses.zh: 既是起誓立的，耶稣就作了更美之约的中保。
verses.en: accordingly Jesus has become the guarantee[NOTE:1] of a better covenant.
notes: Or “surety.”
verses.commentary:
7:22

NASB, NRSV, TEV, REB
"the guarantee"

NKJV, ASV
"the surety"

Peshitta
"its surety"

The Hebrew background is "a pledge put in the hand," which implies surety. It came to be
used in Greek for collateral on a loan or a jail bond. Also, in Roman law it stood for that which was
legally secured. Jesus is the Father's surety of the effectiveness of the New Covenant.

This concept is similar to the usage of the term "seal."

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEAL

▣ "a better covenant" Jer. 31:31-34 speaks of this "New Covenant" (i.e., described in Ezek. 36:22-36) where
the focus is an internal law motivated and produced by the Spirit, not an external code which relies on
human performance. The New Covenant is a grace-based covenant, but humans must respond appropriately both at the
beginning and throughout life!

For "better" see full note at Heb. 7:7.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 那些成为祭司的，数目本来多，是因为有死阻隔，不能长久。
verses.en: And the others[NOTE:1] who became priests were numerous because death prevented them[NOTE:2] from continuing in office,[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “they on the one hand” in contrast with “he on the other hand” in v. 24.
Grk “they were prevented by death.”
Grk “from continuing” (the words “in office” are supplied for clarity).
verses.commentary:
7:23 This is another comparison between Jesus and OT priests. This one deals with the Levitical priests' numbers and
time in office.

verses.zh: 这位既是永远常存的，他祭司的职任就长久不更换。
verses.en: but he holds his priesthood permanently since he lives forever.
verses.commentary:
7:24 This is a rabbinical conclusion based on Genesis 14, where Melchizedek's lineage is not given,
and Psalm 110, which is an allusion to Melchizedek and uses the term "forever" (cf. Ps. 110:4b).

verses.zh: 凡靠着他进到　神面前的人，他都能拯救到底；因为他是长远活着，替他们祈求。
verses.en: So he is able to save completely those who come to God through him because he always lives to intercede for them.
verses.commentary:
7:25

NASB, Peshitta
"to save forever"

NKJV
"to save to the uttermost"

NRSV
"for all time to save"

TEV
"now and always, to save"

NJB
"power to save. . .is absolute"

As the above English translations show, this term has several connotations. He is able to
save completely, all, forever (cf. Heb. 10:14) because He continues "forever" as a better priest.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS AS HIGH PRIEST

▣ "those" This is a universal invitation! Whosoever will may come (cf. John 1:12; 3:16; 6:33,51; Rom. 10:9-13;
2 Cor. 5:19; 1 Tim. 2:4; 4:10; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:2; 4:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "who draw near to God through Him" Jesus is God's plan of redemption (cf. John 10:9; 14:6).
Whosoever will may come (cf. John 1:12; 3:16), but they must come through faith in Him (cf. John 10:7-9; 14:6; 20:31) and
they must continue in faith (PRESENT PARTICIPLE). The Mosaic Covenant was mostly limited to one nation, but
the New Covenant in Jesus fulfills Gen. 3:15 and is open to all the children of Adam (i.e., humanity).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE

▣ "He always lives to make intercession for them" Jesus' work did not end with the cross, but
even today He still prays and pleads for believers at the Father's right hand (cf. Heb. 9:24; Isa. 53:12; Rom. 8:34; 1 John 2:1).

Intercession was part of the ministry of Israel's leaders.

- Abraham

- Moses

- Aaron

- Samuel

- God seeks intercession (Isa. 59:16)

Now our ultimate advocate and intercessor is, Jesus, the Son of God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

verses.zh: 像这样圣洁、无邪恶、无玷污、远离罪人、高过诸天的大祭司，原是与我们合宜的。
verses.en: For it is indeed fitting for us to have such a high priest: holy, innocent, undefiled, separate from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
verses.commentary:
7:26 This is possibly a quote from an early hymn/poem or liturgy (like Phil. 2:6-11; 1 Tim. 3:16;
2 Tim. 2:11-13; and possibly 1 Tim. 1:17; 6:15-16). The term "holy" can mean "merciful" from LXX (cf. Ps. 16:10).

The term "unstained" is a sacrificial term usually translated in the OT as "unblemished." This
is a wonderful confessional summary.

Notice the list of characteristics of Jesus, the High Priest of the New Covenant.

- holy (possibly "merciful" from LXX)

- innocent (sinless)

- undefiled (an acceptable sacrifice; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: BLAMELESS, INNOCENT, GUILTLESS, WITHOUT REPROACH

- separated from sinners (not affected by Adam and Eve's rebellion)

- exalted above the heavens (i.e., ascended; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ASCENSION

These things could not be said of the Levitical priests!

▣ "separated from sinners" This is a PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLE. It does not
reflect on Jesus' humanity (cf. Phil. 2:6-7), but speaks of His sinlessness (cf. Heb. 4:15; 9:14; 2 Cor. 5:21; 1 Pet. 2:22;
1 John 2:1; 3:5).

▣ "exalted above the heavens" This may be

- a statement of preeminence

- a reference to the Gnostic false teachers' view of salvation as passing through the angelic
spheres (i.e., rabbis' levels of heaven; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN, cf. Heb. 4:14)

- a way of referring to the resurrection/ascension (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ASCENSION)

SPECIAL TOPIC: GNOSTICISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: RESURRECTION

SPECIAL TOPIC: ASCENSION

verses.zh: 他不像那些大祭司，每日必须先为自己的罪，后为百姓的罪献祭；因为他只一次将自己献上，就把这事成全了。
verses.en: He has no need to do every day what those priests do, to offer sacrifices first for their own sins and then for the sins of the people, since he did this in offering himself once for all.
verses.commentary:
7:27 This combines the Day of Atonement (cf. Leviticus 16) with the daily temple offerings (the OT continual).
It is historically (i.e., Philo) and rabbinically (i.e., Talmud) verifiable that the high priest was directly involved in daily sacrifices
in later Judaism but possibly not during the days of the tabernacle.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, I. E. #2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS AS HIGH PRIEST

▣ "He offered" This is the same term used in Isa. 53:11 in the Septuagint (LXX), "to bear." Some
see this as an allusion to the smoke of the sacrifices that rose up to God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SOOTHING AROMA

▣ "this He did once for all" Hebrews emphasizes the ultimacy of Jesus' once-given sacrificial
death. This once-done salvation and forgiveness are forever accomplished

- "once" (ephapax), Heb. 7:27; 9:12; 10:10

- "once for all" (hapax), Heb. 6:4; 9:7,26,27,28; 10:2; 12:26,27

This is the recurrent accomplished sacrificial affirmation.

The HIgh Priest and Levitical Priests offered sacrifices again and again, but not Jesus!

▣ "offered up Himself" Jesus is the High Priest (cf. Ps. 110:4) and victim (cf. Isa. 53:11) of
the heavenly sanctuary (cf. Heb. 9:24). This is a pillar of the NT emphasis on substitutionary, vicarious
atonement (cf. Mark 10:45; Rom. 8:3; 2 Cor. 5:21).

Notice Jesus is depicted as

- the High Priest

- a better offering

- once

- Himself

- into the better tabernacle (i.e., heavenly tabernacle)

verses.zh: 律法本是立软弱的人为大祭司；但在律法以后起誓的话，是立儿子为大祭司，乃是成全到永远的。
verses.en: For the law appoints as high priests men subject to weakness,[NOTE:1] but the word of solemn affirmation that came after the law appoints a son made perfect forever.
notes: See Heb 5:2 where this concept was introduced.
verses.commentary:
7:28 "the Law appoints men as high priests who are weak, but the word of the oath, which came after
the Law" This is a contrast between the covenant of Moses and its procedures vs. the "oath" of Ps. 110:4, which
related to the New covenant of Jer. 31:31-34.

▣ "appoints a Son" Jesus is a superior priest because He is part of God's family (i.e.,
"a son,"cf. Heb. 1:2; 3:6; 5:8). This reference seems to combine Ps. 2 and Ps. 110 which were a Royal combined with
a Priestly Psalm. He combines both OT anointed offices (i.e., King and Priest) in Himself by the Father's oath.

▣ "made perfect forever" This is a PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLE. He has been made
perfect (humanly speaking) by suffering and this perfection continues (cf. Heb. 2:10; 5:8-9). This is the counterpoint to
vv. 18,19, where the Levitical High Priest was not "perfect."

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why does the author take so long to develop the concept of Jesus as high priest?

- How is Levi linked to Melchizedek?

- How does Psalm 110 relate to Gen. 14:18-20?

- Why is Melchizedek used as a type of the Messiah?

- Who was Melchizedek?

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS: HEBREWS 8:1-13

- This is part of a unified context related to the reader's need for maturity. This section runs from
Heb. 5:11-10:18 with a parenthesis of warning from Heb. 5:12-6:20.

- Note the use of OT passages

- Hebrews 2 develops using Psalm 8

- Hebrews 3 and 4 develop using Psalm 95

- Hebrews 7 uses Psalm 110

- Hebrews 8 uses Jer. 31:31-34

- Hebrews 10 will use Psalm 40
